cues: Statement announces a rate cut citing global developments and muted inflation, matching the 2019 mid-cycle easing.
The dissenters preferred a range ending at 2 percent, implying 1-3/4 to 2 percent; that was the prevailing range only before the October 2019 cut.
Bullard voted with the majority; in September 2019 he dissented in favor of a larger cut.

The text says the Committee will 'monitor the implications of incoming information... as it assesses the appropriate path', replacing the earlier 'act as appropriate to sustain the expansion' and signaling a pause, as in October 2019.
The description of strong household spending alongside weak business investment and exports fits late 2019.
Two dissents favoring no change fit the pattern of George and Rosengren in 2019.
